name: cipherworkbench
//type: The workspace root itself ships no JS; this is here so vitest.config.ts loads as ESM under Vite's native config loader instead of warning about CommonJS.
description: Cross-platform cipher suite workbench — compute and validate hashes, CRCs, MACs, KDFs and ciphers. Web and desktop.

scripts.build: pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && turbo run build
scripts.//win: Windows launchers, build and packaging scripts, reachable without typing a path. `desktop` above needs the dev server already running; `win:desktop` starts it, waits for port 3000, runs Electron, and stops the server on exit. They shell out to scripts/<area>/*.bat by *relative* path, which is also why they exist: an absolute path to this repo contains parentheses, PowerShell parses those as a subexpression, and a bare path therefore fails with "The term 'Self' is not recognized". No script can fix that. Not needing the path can. Every .bat forwards its arguments, so `pnpm win:package -Release -Verify` reaches create-package.ps1 intact. Note there is no `--` separator: pnpm forwards it literally and PowerShell rejects it as an ambiguous parameter name, which is why every example here omits it.
scripts.//sh: The same launchers, builds and packaging for Linux and macOS. Invoked as `bash scripts/...` by relative path: relative for the same reason the win:* set is, because an absolute path to this repo contains parentheses, and through an explicit `bash` because pnpm runs a script through cmd.exe on Windows, which cannot exec a .sh at all. That prefix costs nothing on Linux and makes the whole set usable from Git Bash on Windows too. Unlike the .bat wrappers these take idiomatic long flags, so `pnpm sh:package --release --verify` works; a bare `--` is dropped by the argument parsers, so the pnpm separator is harmless here rather than fatal as it is on the PowerShell side. Two differ from their Windows counterparts on purpose: sh:build:desktop --package produces the Linux AppImage and .deb rather than the NSIS installer, and sh:icon verifies the committed icons instead of regenerating them, because rasterising the SVG would produce a different icon from the packaged one.
